body.p: Claims 1-58 are pending in this application. Claims 1-58 now stand rejected.
Claims 1-58 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 because the claimed invention is directed to an abstract idea without significantly more.
Applicant respectfully traverses the present rejection for the following reasons. Claim 1 is amended to call for:
wherein the simulated animal data is generated by a method using
a recurrent neural network (RNN) comprising:
(a) receiving real animal data from multiple events, wherein training animal data readings are timestamped and
recorded at predetermined time intervals;
(b) training an untrained recurrent neural network model using the real animal data to form a trained recurrent neural
network model, wherein the training includes: (i) using a sequence of observations as input;
(ii) performing the training over a plurality epochs using an error
metric and an optimizer for updating network weights;
(c) generating simulated animal data by applying the trained neural recurrent network model, wherein the trained recurrent neural network model predicts physiological data including heart rate
based on the real animal data;
(d) performing in-sample forecasting, wherein the simulated animal data is generated from a subset of the real animal data to
predict future values based on known outcomes; and
(e) performing out-of-sample forecasting, wherein the simulated animal data is generated from observations that were not part of the real animal data to predict future values based on
previously unseen data.

Claim 51 is similarly amended. The neural network (RNN) component of claims 1 and 51 are analogous to Example 47, claim 2 the USPTO's July 2024 Subject Matter Eligibility Examples- artificial neural network (ANN) used for detecting malicious network packets which is determined to encompass patent eligible subject matter. The following table summarizes the correlation with

In both claims, the neural network is trained using real data to form a predictive model that is capable of making decisions based on input data. In the malicious network packet detection claim, the ANN is trained using network traffic data and a specific algorithm (backpropagation and gradient descent) to detect anomalies. Similarly, in the animal data claim, the RNN is trained using real animal data (e.g., heart rate) and then used to generate simulated animal data and predict future physiological conditions. Just as the ANN enables detection of anomalies in network traffic to identify malicious packets, the RNN allows the system to detect trends or future physiological outcomes in the animal data. Both systems leverage neural networks to enhance predictive accuracy and move beyond human-driven evaluation.

In the malicious network packet claim, the ANN makes real-time decisions about which packets to block or drop based on detected anomalies. Similarly, in the animal data system, the RNN enables real-time or near real-time analysis of physiological trends and generates artificial data for decision-making and monetization. In amended claim 1, the RNN, like the ANN in the network security claim, supports automated decision-making, where the output of the neural network (simulated animal data) is used for further analysis, potentially leading to real-time actions in health monitoring or other animal-related applications. This automates and enhances the decision-making process in the same way the ANN automatically drops malicious packets.

In the network packet detection claim, the ANN improves the security system by allowing for real-time detection of threats and automated responses, such as dropping malicious packets and blocking future traffic. Similarly, in the animal data system, the RNN improves the data collection system by allowing for the generation of artificial animal data that simulates future outcomes based on real data, enabling better predictions and increasing the value of the data for stakeholders. Just

as the ANN represents a technical improvement in network intrusion detection, the RNN in the animal data system represents a technical improvement in data forecasting and analysis. Both systems improve their respective technical fields by enhancing the ability to manage complex, real-time data and make predictions based on it.

In the malicious network packet claim, the ANN is not just an abstract concept; it is integrated into a larger system that improves network security by detecting anomalies and automatically taking actions to protect the network. In the animal data system, the RNN is similarly integrated into a broader system that collects, processes, and monetizes animal data by generating artificial data for further analysis and decision-making. In both cases, the neural network is not an abstract idea but a crucial part of the overall system that improves its practical utility. In the same way the ANN improves network security by enabling real-time automated responses, the RNN improves the animal data system by enabling more sophisticated data predictions and providing stakeholders with valuable insights for monetization.

The ANN in the network packet detection claim provides a real-world benefit by preventing network intrusions and improving security. Similarly, the RNN in the animal data system provides real-world benefits by predicting animal physiological conditions and enabling stakeholders to monetize the data.

Both systems use neural networks to solve real-world technical problems. In the network packet detection claim, the problem is protecting the network from malicious activity, while in the animal data system, the problem is accurately predicting physiological trends for commercial or health-related applications. In both cases, the neural network enhances the system's ability to manage large amounts of data and make decisions based on it.

In conclusion, the neural network (RNN) component in the animal data claim is patentable because it provides similar benefits and technological improvements as the ANN in the malicious network packet detection claim. Both claims involve the use of a neural network to perform tasks that enhance the functionality of the system, such as real-time predictions, automated decision- making, and improved data handling. The RNN transforms the system for monetizing animal data into a practical, technical application that leverages AI to solve complex, real-world problems in
a manner analogous to the ANN improving network security in the other claim. Therefore, the RNN component contributes significantly to the patentability of the claim.
Accordingly, claims 1-58 are allowable under 35 U.S.C. 101.
